details:
Mission: Possible – Watch Bahrain Grow

Team GADEHA (قدها) | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

Project Overview

Mission: Possible – Watch Bahrain Grow is an interactive, single-player educational game that allows players to experience the process of designing, building, and managing a space mission. Inspired by Bahrain's remarkable geographical transformation, our project combines space engineering, interactive gameplay, and real Earth-observation imagery to make complex scientific concepts accessible and engaging.

Our game challenges players to design a satellite, launch it from Bahrain, and observe how the country's coastline and artificial islands have changed over time.

How the Game Works

Players begin their journey at a futuristic satellite assembly facility in Bahrain, accompanied by Buddy, a friendly astronaut who makes the experience approachable and engaging.

Players select components such as cameras, solar panels, batteries, and communication equipment. Each component influences important mission constraints, including mass, power consumption, and cost.

Players must carefully balance these engineering trade-offs while working within a simulated $1 million mission budget. They then select from three launch vehicles—Light, Medium, or Heavy—each with different payload capacities and costs.

The mission progresses through rocket launch and orbital simulation, culminating in an Earth-observation experience where players compare historical and modern satellite imagery of Bahrain.

Rather than focusing solely on reaching space, the game encourages players to understand how engineering decisions influence mission feasibility and scientific outcomes.

NASA Data Integration

A central feature of our project is the use of historical and modern Earth-observation imagery of Bahrain, including imagery associated with the NASA–USGS Landsat program.

Our game highlights the transformation of Bahrain's coastline through land reclamation and the development of artificial islands, including Durrat Al Bahrain, Amwaj Islands, and Diyar Al Muharraq.

By comparing satellite imagery from different years, players can explore how space-based observations reveal geographical changes that are difficult to appreciate from the ground.

The historical imagery is real Earth-observation data, while the satellite mission and its engineering outcomes are simulated for educational purposes.

Tools and Development

Our team used several technologies to bring the project to life:

  • Unity: Game development, interactive gameplay, user interfaces, and mission simulation.
  • C#: Gameplay logic, component selection, resource calculations, and interactions within Unity.
  • Blender and Python: Custom 3D modeling, environment creation, spacecraft design, and animations.
  • Adobe Illustrator and graphic design tools: Branding, game logo, interface graphics, and visual identity.
  • NASA–USGS Landsat imagery: Historical and modern Earth-observation references for Bahrain's changing coastline.

We developed custom assets, including satellites, three rocket variants, launch infrastructure, the satellite assembly environment, and Buddy, our astronaut guide.

AI-assisted tools, including ChatGPT, supported brainstorming, Blender scripting, debugging, and documentation. These tools were used as development aids, with the resulting work incorporated into our Unity project.

Creativity and Innovation

What distinguishes Mission: Possible is its combination of space mission engineering with a story rooted in Bahrain's geography and heritage.

Our visual identity draws inspiration from Bahrain's artificial islands and pearling history, while our game transforms familiar local developments into an interactive space exploration experience.

We designed Buddy to create an engaging atmosphere for younger audiences and beginners, making technical decision-making feel less intimidating.

Our approach connects the excitement of launching a rocket with the deeper educational value of satellite technology and Earth observation.

Intended Impact and Benefits

Our primary goal is to make space engineering more understandable and engaging for students, young people, and beginners interested in STEM.

Through interactive experimentation, players can develop an appreciation for resource management, engineering constraints, problem-solving, and satellite-based Earth observation.

The project also encourages awareness of Bahrain's geographical development and demonstrates how space technology can help communities understand environmental and urban changes.

Although our initial mission focuses on Bahrain, the concept can be expanded to explore other countries, landscapes, and Earth-observation challenges.

Ultimately, Mission: Possible aims to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and explorers by demonstrating that understanding our planet can begin with a mission to space.
